name: TicketTailor
summary: Low-fee event ticketing and box-office software: sell tickets online, manage check-in and keep more of your revenue without per-ticket booking fees.
best_for: event organizers with their own audience (venues, communities, creators) who want flat low per-ticket fees, full branding and no subscription
skip_if: you depend on marketplace discovery to sell tickets (Eventbrite's traffic is the fee you're paying for), or you run two events a year at tiny volume
honest_knock: The fee honesty is the product: flat cents per ticket instead of percentage skims makes it dramatically cheaper than the big platforms on higher-priced tickets (a $0.30-0.85 fee on a $50 ticket vs a percentage is no contest). The trade: you bring your own audience. There's no discovery marketplace pushing your event, so if you rely on a platform's browsing traffic to sell out, the cheap fees won't fill seats.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-09 and re-read unchanged 2026-09-26 on tickettailor.com/pricing with the currency switched to USD) No subscription and no contract: pay-as-you-sell $0.85 a ticket, or prepaid credits from $0.70 down to $0.34 depending on volume — 100 credits (the minimum) cost $70, 500 cost $300, 1,000 cost $520 and 20,000 cost $6,800. Credits carry no time limit. Free events are free up to 5,000 tickets a year, the first five paid tickets cost nothing, and charities, B Corps, PTAs and not-for-profits get 50% off, as do very low-priced tickets. Seated tickets cost two credits rather than one. Prices switch across GBP, EUR, USD, AUD and CAD. Stripe, PayPal or Square fees apply separately and Ticket Tailor never touches the payment. Note one contradiction in their own FAQ: one answer puts the free-ticket allowance at 5,000 a year, another at 2,000. Re-read on 2026-10-20, when the page served pounds rather than dollars: pay as you go £0.60 a ticket and prepaid from £0.22, both plus VAT, with no fees for up to 5,000 free tickets a year. The help centre's cost article, read the same day, adds the extras billed outside usage: white label at $49 a month (£39, €45) with a custom domain included, or a custom domain alone at $8 a month (£7).

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 5 November 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We created a box office, drafted one event with a ticket type, and read the fee, team and API screens. We published nothing, sold no ticket and connected no payment provider.
findings: Creating the box office asks for an organisation name, country, billing currency, whether tickets are free or paid, and expected yearly volume, plus a tick for the acceptable use policy. No card was asked for.

Billing shows 'Prepay', a credit balance of 5 and Auto-Renew off. Without credits, usage is charged at the pay-as-you-go rate of €0.70, excluding VAT. This is a credit model, so we found no subscription checkout to test.

The ticket dialog showed the fee in advance. For a €12.10 ticket the buyer pays €12.10, estimated fees are €0.43 and you receive €11.67. The €0.70 Ticket Tailor fee is struck through to €0.00 as one trial credit, and the €0.43 is a Stripe example of 1.5% plus €0.25 on a domestic card.

Our draft event kept the accent in 'Zoë' and the two-line description with quotation marks. The kit start date of 28 October is in the past, so we kept the suggested default of 19 November. That is a mapping change on our side, not a data loss.
The event stayed in Draft. 'Get ready to publish' lists a payment method as the open step, and publishing needs a connected payment provider.
Settings > API offers API keys ('Generate a new key') and webhooks on this trial. We created no key.
Team access lists one teammate, the owner. 'Invite teammate' asks for a verification code sent by e-mail first, so we did not see the role options.
not_tested: Roles: the verification step blocked the invite screen, and the code is a step only the account holder can take
Export and re-import: exports need orders, and we found no export for event settings; the second kit record was not entered
Checkout, tax and the final price: we did not open the credit purchase
Support: we found a chat promise on the welcome screen and an API address, but no support mailbox, so we sent no question
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
